Every declaration of a test suite must be partial.

What The Standard says

“Testing” — The Standard separates tests for a subject into focused implementations while keeping them part of one recognizable suite. Partial declarations support that organization without inheritance. read it here.
“Unit Tests” — The canonical controller suite is declared partial, allowing operation-specific test files to share one locally owned fixture. The analyser makes that demonstrated test shape consistent. read it here.

Why it matters

Partial test suites allow one target's many behaviours to be grouped without creating unrelated test classes or an enormous file. The target remains one discoverable suite while setup, validation, exceptions, and operations can be reviewed separately.

Bad code example

// Violates STXTEST004: Every declaration of a test suite must be partial.
class StudentServiceTests { }

Good code example

// Follows STXTEST004
partial class StudentServiceTests { }
